result.rule: When the description says the process begins when an external party uses one of several alternative channels (for example, two different ways of placing the same order), and each channel is described as a separate way of performing that start action: Model each alternative channel as its own task performed by the external party, one task per channel, with no task that combines them. Connect the channel tasks to an exclusive gateway that merges them before the next step of the process, so that exactly one alternative leads onward.

When the description says the process begins with a party's action that can be carried out in one of several alternative ways joined by 'or', and each alternative is work the party performs: Model one start event for the process. Follow it with an exclusive gateway that splits into one task per alternative way, each task performed by that party and named after the action the description gives for that way. Merge those branches with an exclusive gateway before the next described step. Do not model any alternative way as its own start event, and do not drop an alternative.

When the description names two or more alternative ways to carry out the same step, joined by 'or' (for example, the step may be done by one of several named means), and the model would otherwise keep only one of them: Place an exclusive gateway before the alternatives. Give each named alternative its own task on a separate outgoing sequence flow from that gateway, using the action the description names for it. Merge the alternative branches with an exclusive gateway before the next described step. Do not drop any named alternative and do not leave the choice as one unconditional flow.

When the description states that, after a party gives approval or acceptance, the process continues to a named follow-on step, and a later recording or confirmation step depends on that follow-on step: Model the named follow-on step as its own task, placed in the sequence between the approval (an intermediate catch event if it is awaited) and the recording or confirmation step. Do not merge the follow-on step into the approval or into the recording step, and preserve the sequence flows that the description implies.

Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

result.rule: When the description says a work activity is performed until a stated end state or location is reached, and the phrase after 'until' qualifies what the activity does: Keep the qualifying end condition (the phrase introduced by 'until' or an equivalent) in the task label, together with the action verb and its object, so the label says both what work is done and when it stops. Do not shorten the label to a bare verb-object pair when the description attaches that end condition to the activity.

When the description says an activity is carried out continuously, such as watching the status of an item in transit, until a later occurrence is reached, and the description names that activity as work performed by a participant: Model the ongoing activity as its own task (bpmn:task, or a more specific task type if the mode of work is known) in the sequence flow. Model the later occurrence that ends the activity as a separate intermediate catch event that follows it. Do not represent the activity only by the catch event, because the performed work would then be lost.

When the description states an outcome as two passive clauses joined by 'and' in one sentence, with no single actor named for either clause: Model each clause as its own task, labeled with the action the clause names, in the order the description gives, connected by a sequence flow. If the description states the first clause as a prerequisite of the second, place the prerequisite task before the second task. Do not merge the clauses into one task with a joined label, even when one clause summarizes the other.

When the description states a conditional clause (for example 'If ... , ...' or 'after approval ... ') that depends on the result of an earlier activity, and one outcome leads to a different path or to the end of the process: Place an exclusive gateway directly after the activity that produces the outcome. Connect that activity's completion to the gateway, and give each described outcome its own outgoing sequence flow, including the outcome that ends the process or bypasses the following activities. Do not leave the decision as an unconditional flow or omit the gateway.
